plate_findings.evidence: Caption: "circumscribed osteolytic skull lesions in the frontal and occipital regions."
Caption describes an osteolytic lesion of the distal femur assuming a flame or inverted-V shape; the image labels a lytic wedge.
Caption identifies marked thickening of the diploic space associated with circumscribed osteolytic lesions.
Caption describes extensive right hemipelvic involvement with cortical and trabecular remodeling.
Caption: marked cranial table thickening with several areas of focal sclerosis producing a "cotton wool" appearance.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 9 panels (A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, C1, C2, C3, C4). A1: Radiograph from a patient demonstrates circumscribed skull osteolysis characteristic of the lytic phase of Paget disease of bone. [raw subtype: lytic phase] A2: The radiograph shows the characteristic advancing flame-shaped lytic front of the lytic phase. [raw subtype: lytic phase] A3: The proximal progression of a flame-shaped femoral osteolytic lesion supports the lytic phase of Paget disease. [raw subtype: lytic phase] B1: The coexistence of skull osteolysis and diploic thickening is characteristic of the mixed remodeling phase of Paget disease. [raw subtype: mixed phase] B2: The pelvic radiograph shows mixed cortical and trabecular remodeling typical of mixed-phase Paget disease. [raw subtype: mixed phase] C1: Focal calvarial sclerosis with the captioned cotton-wool appearance is characteristic of late Paget disease. panels.figure_caption: Radiological presentation of Paget’s disease of Bone. A Lytic phase. Upper panel: circumscribed osteolytic skull lesions in the frontal and occipital regions. Lower panels: osteolytic lesions of the distal femur progressing proximally and assuming the shape of a flame or inverted V. B Mixed phase. Upper panel: circumscribed osteolytic skull lesions, associated with marked thickening of the diploic space; lower panel: extensive involvement in the right hemipelvis with areas of cortical (ilio-pectineal and ilio-ischial lines) and trabecular thickening and circumscribed osteolytic lesions. C Blastic, osteosclerotic phase. Upper panel: marked thickening of the cranial table, particularly the inner calvarial table, together with several areas of focal sclerosis (“cotton wool” appearance) [right]; compression fracture (CF) at a sclerotic pagetic vertebra [left]. Lower panels: pagetic tibias in blastic phase, with diffuse cortical thickening, trabecular osteosclerosis (causing a loss of distinction between cortex and medulla), bone enlargement and deformity. In the right panel is shown a transverse fissure fracture (FF)
